newsitem.title: INDONESIA: At least 26 dead in Indonesian plane crash.
newsitem.headline: At least 26 dead in Indonesian plane crash.

text.p: At least 26 people died and 26 others where injured when an Indonesian plane clipped the rooftops of a housing complex and crashed into a field near this west Java hill city on Thursday, witnesses and officials said.
Two of the 26 injured were residents of the housing estate, an official at the national search and rescue organisation in Jakarta told Reuters.

Transport Minister Haryanto Dhanutirto told reporters at the site the pilot was apparently attempting an emergency landing at a nearby military airfield as the Sempati Air Fokker F-27 lost power after taking off from Bandung for Jakarta.
The rescue official said the plane's manifest showed it was carrying 50 passengers and crew. Earlier police reports said there were 51 people on board, including a baby.
The official Antara news agency said one of the dead was a Singaporean it identified as Johnny Koh Eng.
Eyewitnesses said the Dutch-made twin-engined turboprop Fokker clipped roofs and a wall of a housing complex about 13 km (eight miles) from Bandung and crashed into a muddy field beside the houses.
Wreckage was strewn across the field.
"I saw the plane circling and flying at an angle before I heard a boom, and it came down and crashed," said Sunarso, who told Reuters he had helped pull five people from the wreckage.

The dead and injured were initially taken to the airbase hospital about one km (half a mile) away, where Lieutenant Hendri told Reuters he had sent 26 bodies to the Hasan Sadikin general hospital in Bandung.

Transport Minister Haryanto told reporters the pilot had asked for permission to return to Bandung airport after an engine failure, but it appeared he was attempting an emergency landing at the airbase about five km (three miles away) when the plane crashed.
An official at Bandung's Immanuel private hospital said 21 people, including two thought to be Malaysians, were being treated.
Other victims were believed to be at other hospitals in the area.
An airport official at Bandung's Husein Sastranegara airport said the plane crashed nine minutes after take-off on its flight to Jakarta, 120 km (75 miles) to the northwest.
There was no immediate comment from Sempati Air officials.

Indonesia, spread along the equator and comprising about 17,500 islands, relies heavily on air transport, although international aviation experts are often critical of the standard of training and maintenance practices in its aviation sector.

In January 1996, 15 people died when a trainer plane crashed into a Bandung suburb, but the death toll in Thursday's accident is the highest since 18 people died last December when a CASA C-212 crashed into a factory in South Kalimantan.
Last week, three crew died when a recently repaired Merpati Nusantara Airlines (MNA) Spanish-designed CASA C-212 crashed in eastern Indonesia.
In April, 15 people died when a British-made ATP plane also operated by MNA crashed on Belitung island.
In May, a locally built CN-235 military transport aircraft crashed during a test flight killing all six crew.
